nodes.notes: One trigger, both update types. Telegram allows a single webhook per bot: a second trigger anywhere does not share it, it takes it, and the first then receives nothing at all.

nodes.notes: Same payload shape as the chat trigger, so any of the three branches can be exercised without touching the bot.

nodes.name: Route the update
nodes.notes: A button, a command, or somebody replying to an arrival notice. Everything the bot receives comes through here.

nodes.notes: Everything an operator changes lives here. Spreadsheet id and chat id are the two that must.

nodes.notes: The links are built from the base URL in Settings, so a fork hands out its own addresses.

nodes.notes: Reads the sample id out of the message the grader replied to. No session state, no commands.

nodes.name: Can assess?
nodes.notes: A sample that never arrived cannot be assessed, and one already assessed is not quietly reassessed.

nodes.name: Look up spec rows
nodes.notes: Every parameter row for this spec, in store order, which is contract order.

nodes.name: Build extraction request
nodes.notes: The prompt is generated from the spec rows. Add a parameter to the sheet and the model is asked for it.

nodes.name: Transcribe the recording
nodes.notes: Off until an endpoint is set. Anything speech to text that takes a file and returns text fits here.

nodes.notes: Without this the model receives the string 'filesystem-v2' where an image should be, and every reading comes back not stated.

nodes.name: Build vision request
nodes.notes: The prompt comes from the spec rows. The image arrives already base64, from the node before it.

nodes.name: Read the grading sheet
nodes.notes: One job: turn what is written on the sheet into the named values the spec asks for.

nodes.name: Build text request
nodes.notes: The same prompt over typed text or over a transcript, so both are read by identical instructions.

nodes.name: Read the typed reading
nodes.notes: Extraction only. Nothing downstream of here asks a model for an opinion.

nodes.name: Parse extraction
nodes.notes: Fails closed. Output that is not JSON is not retried softer and not half salvaged.

nodes.name: Verdict engine
nodes.notes: The model transcribes and extracts. It does not decide. This node decides, the same way every time.

nodes.name: Build assessment update
nodes.notes: The transcript is written whether or not the parse worked. It is what gets argued about later.

nodes.name: Record the assessment
nodes.notes: Writes only what an assessment is allowed to write.

nodes.notes: A button press is a different job with a different guard, so it stays a separate workflow. It cannot have its own trigger: the bot has one webhook and this trigger owns it.

parameters.content:
## Flow C: Evaluation

Voice, a photo of the grading sheet, or typed text in. Named values out, then a verdict.

Voice needs a transcription endpoint, which is a separate service. Leave it blank and the workflow says so rather than guessing.

The chat trigger ships **disabled**: enabling it repoints your bot webhook. The webhook beside it takes the same payload for testing.

## The model reads. It does not decide.

The model turns a voice note, a photographed grading sheet or a typed message into named values with a confidence on each. That is its whole job.

The verdict is the Code node below: fixed rules, compared against thresholds someone typed into the spec store. A rejected lot is a commercial argument, so it has to reason identically every time.

**Swap the model, and the verdicts do not move.**

The engine has no clock, no random source and no network. Give it the same reading and the same spec and it returns the same verdict, in the same order, a year later.

nodes.name: Note: The model reads. It does not decide.

parameters.content:
## Your parameters, not ours

The spec store holds **one row per quality parameter**, not one row per contract:

`param, label, unit, check, direction, threshold, values, tolerance_pct, required`

Two kinds of check cover a quality clause:
- **numeric**: a value against a threshold, one direction. Moisture at most 12.0. Protein at least 11.5.
- **absent**: a condition that must not be present at all. No tolerance applies to something the contract excludes by name.

The prompt is generated from these rows, so the model is asked for exactly the parameters your contract states. **Adding a parameter is a row. It is never a change to a node.**
